summary_en: Introduces an automated signal-domain speed-of-sound compensation framework for hemispherical 3D PACT. The method extracts irregular acoustic boundaries directly from raw 1024-element array measurements using robust channel-adaptive thresholds, constructs an equivalent dual-speed-of-sound propagation model, and corrects wavefront distortion without manual segmentation or auxiliary ultrasound hardware. Validation includes simulations, irregular phantoms, and in vivo mouse imaging.
publication_note: High-confidence reconstruction-method backfill. Strongly aligned with computational photoacoustic imaging and should be promoted to the main library.

summary_en: Studies how repeated laser excitation and transient thermal accumulation affect functional PAM oxygen-saturation accuracy. The paper derives a practical maximum-fluence relation for repeated-pulse imaging and validates it in a blood phantom and mouse brain, providing an acquisition-design constraint for quantitative high-speed functional PAM.
publication_note: High-confidence functional-PAM acquisition/accuracy paper. It is less reconstruction-centric than the 3D SoS-compensation paper but still belongs in the main photoacoustic imaging library because it establishes a quantitative acquisition limit that directly affects image validity.
